briefing.headline: Bold claim is our highest-volume hook but runs 13% below account median across 55 posts, story and announcement framing run 20% above it and are the clearest single fix available.

do_more.point: Lead with breaking incidents and named attacks. Incident/news outperforms product feature posts on every platform and produces the highest individual post reach by far.
do_more.evidence: PyPI malicious-package post hit 12.67x on LinkedIn; OpenAI lawsuit post hit 4.33x. Incident/news averaged 1.05x vs product feature at 0.91x over 30 days.

do_more.point: Use images more. Image posts ran 1.23x account normal with 43% breaking out, well above text at 0.98x with 13% breakout.
do_more.evidence: Devcon image hit 11.79x; Pearl partner image hit 5.74x. 21 image posts averaged 1.23x over 120 days vs 223 text posts at 0.98x.

do_more.point: Post on Sunday or Saturday, not Friday. Sunday averaged 1.34x in 30 days with 45% breakout. Friday averaged 0.87x. The weekend advantage held over 120 days.
do_more.evidence: Sunday: 1.34x (30 days), 1.24x (120 days). Friday: 0.87x (30 days), 0.92x (120 days). Gap is consistent and large across both windows.

do_more.point: Use announcement hooks when the goal is clicks. Announcement reaches 1.06x AND drives 9.8 clicks per 1k, highest of any hook for sending people to 1Claw.
do_more.evidence: Announcement: 1.06x, 9.8 clicks/1k. Bold claim: 0.87x, 3.8 clicks/1k. Announcement wins on both reach and traffic simultaneously.

stop.point: Stop the eco-spotlight, pillars, and themed automated workflows. They account for 50+ posts and hit zero breakout posts across both time windows.
stop.evidence: eco-spotlight: 0.83-0.86x, 0% breakout. pillars: 0.78-0.79x, 0% breakout. themed: 0.71-0.86x, 0% breakout. All confirmed in both 30 and 120-day windows.

stop.point: Stop using bold claim as the default hook. It's the most-used hook by far but runs at 0.87x and 9% breakout, it is the main drag on weekly performance.
stop.evidence: Bold claim (55 posts): 0.87x, 9% breakout. Story (29 posts): 1.08x, 34% breakout. The gap is 0.21x. Bottom LinkedIn posts all use this pattern.

stop.point: Stop casual personal one-liners on @DevSecOpz. They don't reach builders or security people and have no connection to 1Claw's audience.
stop.evidence: 'Classic.' hit 0.31x. 'Picked up a @wedgiedev today' hit 0.44x. Only 7% of X engagers over 30 days were builders, security pros, or founders.

stop.point: Stop contest-verification posts from @DevSecOpz. They hit 0.47x and contest activity is filling the funnel with crypto accounts, not builders.
stop.evidence: DevSecOpz verification post: 0.47x. Contest engagement on X (30 days): 52 crypto accounts, 7 bots, 6 builders. Wrong audience for a security infrastructure product.

test_next.point: Test partner/community posts on Kevin's LinkedIn deliberately, 4-6 posts over two weeks announcing integrations or ecosystem moves.
test_next.why: Niche competitors hit 1.67x on partner/community (18 posts); our LinkedIn partner posts average 0.83x in 30 days. @e2b and @browserbase both broke out with partner announcements (3.6x, 1.88x). The gap is real and untested on our LinkedIn.

test_next.point: Test how-to/list hook posts with a specific numbered technique on @1clawAI (e.g. '3 ways prompt injection bypasses guardrails'). Measure clicks per 1k, not reach.
test_next.why: How-to/list hook drives 9.9 clicks/1k, second only to announcement. Only 7% of our X engagers are builders or security people; converting the ones we do reach matters more than chasing raw reach.

test_next.point: Test incident/news posts on @1clawAI as short video, a screen recording of the attack, a news clip, 30-60 seconds.
test_next.why: Incident/news topic averages 1.05x; video format averages 1.06x in 30 days. The Pearl product video hit 6.66x. The incident + video combination hasn't been run deliberately and both signals point up.

writer_rules: Open with what just happened, not what it means: 'Yesterday, attackers pushed...' not 'AI agents have never been more vulnerable.'
Name the specific attack, company, or count in the first sentence, the top posts (PyPI, OpenAI lawsuit, Pearl) all do this; the bottom posts don't.
On X: use story or announcement framing to open, not a bold claim. Story and announcement run 0.21x higher than bold claim across 55 recent posts.
On LinkedIn: put the incident name and a number in line 1. 'Yesterday, attackers pushed…190,000 downloads' hit 12.67x; 'AI is moving fast and so are the hackers' posts hit 0.33x.
Cut generic urgency phrases: 'there has never been a more important time' and 'AI is moving fast and so are the hackers' both appear directly in bottom posts.
briefing.caveats: LinkedIn lift uses reactions and comments as a proxy for reach (no view data), making it incomparable to X or TikTok; TikTok has only 12 posts and is directional only; posts from the last 10 days are still collecting views and may shift materially before next week's read.
